title: Dark-grey painted timber bevel-back weatherboards (Ngaio, Wellington)
jurisdiction: New Zealand (MBIE, Building Act 2004): comparative test only; not an Alberta case; no Alberta applicability asserted
code_edition: NZ Building Code B2/E2 with E2/AS1 as cited
document_type: MBIE determination under Building Act 2004 s188 (regulator decision on an individual matter); not an applicant's alternative-solution file

facts.text: Authority's concern: the installed weatherboards may not comply with B2.3.1 because the dark paint colour may cause cupping and splitting; the matter is whether they complied with B2 as it relates to E2 as originally installed.
Upper level re-clad with 187 × 18 mm H3.1 bevel-back Pinus radiata weatherboards (155 mm cover, 32 mm lap) on a 20 mm cavity over a 15 mm H3.2 plywood rigid air barrier.
Paint described by the manufacturer as a 'cool colour'; applicant reported TSR 25%, while the weatherboard manufacturer required TSR of 40% or more and a warranty statement.
Consent SR 442662 issued 12 July 2019; final inspection failed 13 March 2020; CCC suspended pending a manufacturer statement; house later sold and repainted before determination.

Discussion weighs exposure and shading, access, maintenance documentation and the E2/AS1 note on dark-painted tangentially-sawn weatherboards; decision states it is case-specific and lists factors to be considered individually.

limitations: Comparative only: a New Zealand determination used to test attachment format and content; it cannot establish Alberta performance or applicability.
